title: Gapminder Analysis in Python
text:
Data: [Gapminder] (www.gapminder.org)

#Import Dataframe
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

gapminder = pd.read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/data-raw/08_gap-every-five-years.tsv", sep="\t")
gapminder_subset = gapminder[(gapminder["country"] == "Canada") | (gapminder["country"] == "Japan")]


# Calculate and select total GDP of Canada and Japan
gapminder_subset = gapminder_subset.copy()
gapminder_subset["total_gdp"] = gapminder_subset["gdpPercap"] * gapminder_subset["pop"]

gdp_summary = (
    gapminder_subset
    .groupby(["country", "year"], as_index=False)["total_gdp"]
    .sum()
)
gdp_summary["total_gdp_trillion"] = gdp_summary["total_gdp"] / 10**12


# Plot Total GDP of Canada and Japan over time
fig, ax = plt.subplots()

for country, group in gdp_summary.groupby("country"):
    ax.plot(group["year"], group["total_gdp_trillion"], marker="o", linewidth=2, label=country)

ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Total GDP (trillions USD)")
ax.set_title("figure 1: \nTotal GDP: Canada vs. Japan")
ax.legend(title="Country")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Total GDP (in trillions USD) of Canada and Japan over time.






# Plot GDP per capita of Canada and Japan over time
fig, ax = plt.subplots()

for country, group in gapminder_subset.groupby("country"):
    ax.plot(group["year"], group["gdpPercap"], marker="o", linewidth=2, label=country)

ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("GDP per Capita")
ax.set_title("figure 2: \nGDP per Capita: Canada vs. Japan")
ax.legend(title="Country")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 2: GDP per capita of Canada and Japan over time.





I used gapminder dataset to compare the economic growth between Canada and Japan.
First I multiplied the GDP per-capita by population to obtain Canada and Japan’s total GDP in trillion USD. Then I visualized the comparison of total GDP and GDP per-capita of both countries over years. From figure 1 , I found Japan’s total GDP has been growing rapidly and always greater than Canada’s total GDP.
However, this does not imply that the economy in Japan grew faster than Canada once I look into figure 2: the comparison of GDP per capita. Both countries had similar GDP per-capita and Canada’s GDP per-capita overtook Japan’s for most of the time.

title: Gapminder Analysis in R
text:
Data: [Gapminder] (www.gapminder.org)

# Import Dataframe
library(gapminder)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

gapminder_subset <- subset(gapminder, country %in% c("Canada", "Japan"))


# Calculate and select total GDP of Canada and Japan
gapminder_subset <- gapminder_subset |>
  mutate(total_gdp = gdpPercap * pop)

gdp_summary <- gapminder_subset |>
  group_by(country, year) |>
  summarise(total_gdp = sum(total_gdp), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(total_gdp_trillion = total_gdp / 10^12) 


# Plot Total GDP of Canada and Japan over time
ggplot(gdp_summary, aes(x = year, y = total_gdp_trillion, color = country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Total GDP (trillions USD)",
    color = "Country",
    title = "figure 1: \nTotal GDP: Canada vs. Japan"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()







Figure 1: Total GDP (in trillions USD) of Canada and Japan over time.






# Plot GDP per capita of Canada and Japan over time
ggplot(gapminder_subset, aes(x = year, y = gdpPercap, color = country)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "GDP per Capita",
    color = "Country",
    title = "figure 2: \nGDP per Capita: Canada vs. Japan"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()







Figure 2: GDP per capita of Canada and Japan over time.





I used gapminder dataset to compare the economic growth between Canada and Japan.
First I multiplied the GDP per-capita by population to obtain Canada and Japan’s total GDP in trillion USD. Then I visualized the comparison of total GDP and GDP per-capita of both countries over years. From figure 1 , I found Japan’s total GDP has been growing rapidly and always greater than Canada’s total GDP.
However, this does not imply that the economy in Japan grew faster than Canada once I look into figure 2: the comparison of GDP per capita. Both countries had similar GDP per-capita and Canada’s GDP per-capita overtook Japan’s for most of the time.
